/whyTourWorks/routeLogicSections/0/items.source_en: Free admission at almost every stop — only ⟦G0⟧ is ₩2,000

Oedolgae & Olle Route 7, Yakcheonsa, O'sulloc, and ⟦G0⟧ are all free, and only the ⟦G1⟧ admission (adult ₩2,000) is included in the base price. Unlike most Jeju group tours, which charge ₩15,000–₩20,000 per person in separate admissions, the only real extra cost on the day is lunch (~₩15,000).

The operator publishes an explicit no-shopping clause — there are no ginseng shops, cosmetic-mall detours, or commission lunch stops. Every stop on the route is an actual attraction. The Dongmun Market drop-off is self-guided after the tour ends, not a forced stop.
A route that starts on the coast and finishes on Hallasan

See the Seogwipo coast (⟦G0⟧, Oedolgae) early in the morning before the tour buses arrive, pass through the temple, lunch and tea field, then cross Hallasan via Route 1100 at the end of the day back to Jeju City. A counter-clockwise loop that never retraces the same road.

The shared mini-coach format keeps groups small enough for personal guide attention on the Oedolgae Olle trail and within the Yakcheonsa grounds. Unlike large commission-bus tours (30–40 people), this runs closer to 12–18 — the sweet spot for ample attention without paying private-tour rates.

/whyTourWorks/routeLogicSections/0/title.source_en: Why this route is built this way

/routeShapeIntro/subtitle.source_en: A counter-clockwise route that descends in the morning to the southern Seogwipo coast for ⟦G1⟧ and Oedolgae & the Olle Trail, passes East Asia's largest ⟦G0⟧ and lunch and the O'sulloc Tea Museum, then crosses Hallasan via Route 1100 at the end of the day to finish on the Eoseungsaengak Trail. A day designed to take in waterfall, coast, temple, tea field, and volcano all at once.

/staticQuestions/0/answer.source_en: Yes. This route runs every day of the year. The atmosphere of the Seogwipo coast and the Hallasan views change with the season, but the day's pacing stays the same. In winter snow, ⟦G0⟧ may be substituted for a lower-elevation alternate.

/staticQuestions/1/answer.source_en: At ⟦G1⟧ you go down and back up about 130 steps to the foot of the falls, and ⟦G0⟧ is a 1.3 km one-way wooden-stair climb (about 60–75 min round-trip). Comfortable closed-toe sneakers are enough — no technical hiking gear required. This route does not include the Hallasan summit (Baengnokdam) climb.

/staticQuestions/1/question.source_en: Is the walking at ⟦G0⟧ and Hallasan difficult?

It is a south Jeju signature route that starts on the Seogwipo coast and finishes on Hallasan.

/staticQuestions/6/question.source_en: Is this a good choice for first-time visitors to southern Jeju?

/staticQuestions/7/answer.source_en: It is an active day with the ⟦G1⟧ stairs and the ⟦G0⟧ climb, but the Oedolgae Olle trail and Yakcheonsa and O'sulloc are relatively flat.

/staticQuestions/8/answer.source_en: It suits families with children who can handle a full day of moving around. The coastal walks and the temple and tea field are easy for kids to enjoy too.

/staticQuestions/8/question.source_en: Is this tour suitable for families?

/staticQuestions/9/answer.source_en: Recommended for active seniors comfortable with the ⟦G0⟧ stairs and the Eoseungsaengak climb. Oedolgae, Yakcheonsa, and O'sulloc are relatively comfortable.

/staticQuestions/10/answer.source_en: Best fit is around age 10 and up — children who can handle a full-day itinerary and the walking notes above.
